title: The Waiting Driver
brief: At Meridian Logistics a subcontracted driver is waiting at dock 4 to take a load to a supermarket regional centre with a 6 a.m. booking slot. The final dispatch check shows the load is 3 cases short against the order. The dispatcher proposes sending it "and sorting the paperwork tomorrow". You have 12 visit points to decide.

actions.label: General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: Who can authorize a short shipment
A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: Final dispatch check FD-221 shows 3 cases short; the "released" box is ticked by the dispatcher.
evidence.whyItMatters: Release with a known discrepancy needs authorization.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read the check against the release tick.

evidence.text: Dispatch procedure DP-1 requires the shift manager to authorize short shipments and inform the customer.
Dispatcher: "If we miss the slot we get fined. Nobody counts 3 cases." (note 1)
evidence.whyItMatters: Pressure must not replace authorization and customer communication.

evidence.text: Shift manager can authorize and is on site.
Customer terms CT-4 require advance shipping notice of any shortage before departure.
Stock: "3 cases are in reserve location R-12; 15 minutes to fetch."
Driver: "I can wait 30 minutes and still make 6 a.m." (log DR-5)
Truck is an approved type for the load.
Order status shows "complete" in the system (order OS-221).
evidence.missedExplanation: Compare system status with the check.

evidence.text: Pallet labels on the load match the order.

options: Untick the release, fetch the 3 cases from R-12 within the driver's 30 minutes, re-check, and release; if not possible, have the shift manager authorize a short shipment and send the advance notice
decisions.rationale: The order can be completed in time; if not, the defined route and customer notice apply.
optionFeedback: Ships a known discrepancy without authority or notice.
Completes the order or follows the defined route.

decisions.prompt: How do you respond to "nobody counts 3 cases"?
options: Explain calmly that the customer's terms require notice, and show that fetching the cases fits within the time
decisions.rationale: Facts and a practical route address the pressure.

containment: Untick release and set order status back to pending
correction: Complete the order from R-12 and re-check
cause: The system allows release and "complete" status with an open discrepancy
corrective: Block release with open discrepancies unless authorized and notified
effectiveness: Audit dispatch checks weekly for two months

debriefText.found: You completed the order within the time available.
debriefText.missed: Ask whether the missing goods are available nearby.
debriefText.falseFinding: The truck type and the clock are conforming.
